plan.summary: This first 4-week block is a simple off-camp build for boxing with one weekly S&C session using bodyweight only. Week 1 establishes a baseline on the primary lower-body lift so future work can be judged against it, and the main training starts in Week 2. With only one session per week and a preference for more conditioning, each day keeps a power-first flow, adds practical strength work, then finishes with short conditioning.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build basic lower-body strength, trunk stiffness, and simple explosive qualities while keeping conditioning support in the session.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress single-leg strength and explosive output with slightly denser conditioning while keeping recovery manageable.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep strength with a lower dose and express it faster through sharper jumps, faster bodyweight work, and fresh conditioning.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump as high and fast as you can. Stick each landing softly and rest long enough to keep every rep crisp.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if repeated countermovement timing feels uncoordinated. Start from a still quarter squat and jump hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe surface if you have one. Step down each rep and keep the landing quiet.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up with easier split-squat sets, then build to one hard top set per side with clean form. Log reps and difficulty to set your baseline for the next block. Use a regular split squat if you do not have a safe rear-foot support height.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively with controlled split-squat sets, then perform one hard top set of 3-5 reps per side with your chosen variation. Log the variation, reps, and effort so future work can be compared against this baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track the hardest clean set per side this week and use the same setup next time.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you do not have a stable rear-foot support. Keep the front foot flat and torso tall.

substitutionOptions.name: Assisted Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Hold a wall or door frame lightly if balance is the main limiter. Keep the work in the front leg.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stop with 1-2 clean reps in reserve. Keep ribs down, body straight, and press the floor away hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use hands on a bench, couch, or sturdy surface if floor push-ups are too hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Knee Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this only if needed to keep clean full-range reps.

exercises.name: Towel Row
exercises.notes: Use a sturdy anchored setup only. Pull elbows back, pause briefly at the top, and keep your body braced throughout.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a stable heavy table only if it is completely secure.

substitutionOptions.name: Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Load a backpack if you need a safer simple row option. Keep the torso fixed and row with control.

exercises.name: Side Plank
exercises.notes: Make a straight line from head to heel. Drive the floor away and do not let the hips sag.

substitutionOptions.name: Front Plank
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if side plank positioning is too difficult. Keep abs tight and glutes on.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Conditioning Intervals
exercises.notes: Stay sharp, light, and technically clean. This is conditioning support, not sloppy fatigue work.

endurancePrescription.rest: 1 minute easy walk and nasal breathing between rounds

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Jump high with full intent. Stop if height drops off or landings get noisy.

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want a simpler jump pattern with less timing demand.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low safe box if available. Step down and keep each rep clean.

exercises.name: Split Squat
exercises.notes: Use a controlled lower, slight pause at the bottom, and drive up hard. Leave 2 reps in reserve on every set.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track whether all sets stay smooth with 2 reps left in reserve before progressing reps or difficulty.

substitutionOptions.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a stable support and want a harder version.

substitutionOptions.name: Assisted Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use light support for balance if needed so the legs do the work.

exercises.name: Push-Up
exercises.notes: Stop with 1-2 clean reps in reserve. Keep the neck neutral and the whole body tight.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands if you cannot keep full-range clean reps.

substitutionOptions.name: Tempo Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a 3-second lower if regular push-ups are too easy but external load is not available.

exercises.name: Backpack Row
exercises.notes: Brace the torso, pull the bag toward the hip, and squeeze the upper back without twisting.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a secure anchored setup if that is more practical.

substitutionOptions.name: Table Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use only if the setup is very stable and safe.

exercises.name: Reverse Crunch
exercises.notes: Curl the pelvis up under control. Do not swing the legs or let the low back arch hard.

substitutionOptions.name: Strict Leg Raise
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you have a safe hanging setup and can control the movement.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if trunk control is the limiter and reverse crunches are too sloppy.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Conditioning Intervals
exercises.notes: Work at a steady hard pace while keeping the hands fast and the feet organized.

endurancePrescription.rest: 45 seconds easy walk and shakeout between rounds

exercises.name: Skater Jump
exercises.notes: Cover a manageable distance and stick each landing before the next rep. Stay athletic and balanced, not rushed.

substitutionOptions.name: Skater Hop to Stick
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this lower-output version if balance or landing control is still developing.

substitutionOptions.name: Countermovement Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if lateral jumping irritates anything or space is tight.

exercises.name: Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
exercises.notes: Control the descent, keep the front foot planted, and drive up with intent. Leave 1-2 reps in reserve.

performanceTarget.prompt: Track whether you can keep all sets controlled with 1-2 reps left in reserve at the same setup.

substitutionOptions.name: Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the rear-foot-elevated setup is not stable.

substitutionOptions.name: Assisted Rear-Foot-Elevated Split Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use light support if balance is limiting the leg work.

exercises.name: Close-Grip Push-Up
exercises.notes: Hands just inside shoulder width. Keep elbows under control and stop before form breaks.

substitutionOptions.name: Standard Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the close-grip position bothers the wrists or shoulders.

substitutionOptions.name: Incline Close-Grip Push-Up
substitutionOptions.notes: Raise the hands if you need an easier version with clean form.

exercises.name: Backpack Row
exercises.notes: Use a steady tempo and full range. If the load is light, pause for 1 second at the top of each rep.

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a secure anchor if that gives you a better pulling challenge.

substitutionOptions.name: One-Arm Backpack Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use one arm at a time if you need more loading from a light backpack.

exercises.name: Hollow Body Hold
exercises.notes: Press the low back gently into the floor and keep the ribs down. Shorten the lever if you lose position.

substitutionOptions.name: Dead Bug
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you cannot hold a strong hollow shape yet.

substitutionOptions.name: Reverse Crunch
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if a dynamic trunk drill feels better than an isometric hold.

exercises.name: Shadow Boxing Conditioning Intervals
exercises.notes: Push the pace but keep mechanics sharp. Fast hands and clean footwork matter more than flailing.

exercises.name: Countermovement Jump

substitutionOptions.name: Squat Jump

substitutionOptions.name: Towel Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a secure anchor if that is more practical.
